sections.h2: What should a seller know about Panama City, Florida?
sections.html:
Panama City is a Florida Panhandle city on St. Andrews Bay, about 95 miles east of Pensacola and 100 miles southwest of Tallahassee. The city's own site says the bay surrounds much of town and shelters the harbor at the Port of Panama City.

The same page gives an average annual temperature of 68.8 degrees and about 57.86 inches of rain a year. Salt air, humidity and storm season all work on roofs, siding and windows, so condition matters to buyers here.

Storm repair history is part of the story of many Gulf Coast houses, so keep contractor invoices, permits and insurance claim records together before you sell. Buyers and insurers ask about roof age and past claims.

sections.h2: What neighborhoods and amenities affect a Panama City sale?
sections.html:
Water access is the headline feature. The city lists public boat ramps at St. Andrews Marina, Downtown Marina, Carl Gray Park, Snug Harbor and Bob George Park, plus waterfront parks such as Adams, Asbell, Calhoun Beach and Millville Waterfront.

  • St. Andrews, Downtown and Millville are linked by a mural trail with more than 15 exhibits.
  • The city counts eight walking trails, 13 playgrounds and 20 multipurpose fields.
  • Downtown has the Center for the Arts and the Martin Theatre.

Proximity to these places shows up in how buyers value a house. A home near the marinas or the arts district has a different buyer pool than an inland lot, and an honest listing or offer conversation should reflect that.

sections.h2: Which permits matter when selling in Panama City?
sections.html:
The city requires permits before work starts on roofs, decks, sheds, remodels and electrical, plumbing, mechanical and structural changes. It says the owner or the owner's agent must make sure required permits are issued.

Permits lapse if work does not begin within 6 months or stops for 6 months, and a certificate of occupancy or completion closes out the work. Building Services is at 501 Harrison Ave., phone 850-872-3025.

If you repaired storm damage, confirm every project was closed. An open permit is a common source of delay at a title company, and a cash buyer will usually discount for it.

sections.h2: When do Bay County taxes come due, and what discounts apply?
sections.html:
Bay County tax notices normally go out on or before November 1 with a due date of March 31, and anything unpaid is delinquent April 1. The county tax collector's page lists the early payment schedule below.

Bay County early payment discounts for real estate tax
Month paidDiscount
November4 percent
December3 percent
January2 percent
February1 percent

Non-ad valorem charges for paving, stormwater and solid waste are collected on the same timetable. The tax collector has offices at 850 W. 11th St. in Panama City and elsewhere in the county. If you sell mid year, the closing agent splits the bill between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: How does homestead affect a Panama City home sale?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption of up to $50,000 is available on a permanent residence. The first $25,000 applies to all taxes, including school taxes, and the additional amount applies to non-school taxes on value over $50,000.

File with the Bay County Property Appraiser by March 1. Save Our Homes limits yearly increases to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change, but a sale resets the assessed value to just value the following January 1.

  • Rented homes lose homestead.
  • Portability lets you carry savings to a new Florida home within three years.
  • Seniors may qualify for extra exemptions if the local ordinance allows.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Bay County?
sections.html:
Florida deed stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration under the statute, and the Department of Revenue says all parties are liable. The county clerk collects it at recording.

Clerk recording charges are $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus a modernization fee and a per page technology charge. Ask your closing agent for the full number. If the home carries a mortgage, the consideration includes what the buyer takes subject to.

sections.h2: How can seniors and veterans reduce a Panama City tax bill?
sections.html:
Age 65 or older owners may qualify for an additional homestead exemption of up to $50,000 if a local ordinance allows it and household income is within the limit. The state also lists a $5,000 reduction for disabled ex-servicemembers and a homestead discount for veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability.

Total and permanent disability can lead to a full homestead exemption. Ask the Bay County Property Appraiser which of these apply to you.

  • Apply by March 1 for the tax year.
  • Appeal a denial to the value adjustment board within 30 days of the letter.
  • Value challenges go to the clerk within 25 days of the TRIM notice.

sections.h2: What happens if taxes go unpaid on a Panama City house?
sections.html:
After April 1 delinquency, tax certificates are sold by June 1. The holder can apply for a tax deed after two years, and the opening bid on homestead property includes half of the latest assessed value.

If the house is yours and you are behind, sell or pay before an application is filed. Get a payoff from the Bay County Tax Collector, which accepts delinquent payments in certified funds, including cash, cashier's check, money order or credit card.

sections.h2: What if the Panama City house is inherited, tenant occupied or in foreclosure?
sections.html:
Each has a statutory clock. Estates up to $150,000 non-exempt may use summary administration, tenants get a 3 day notice for unpaid rent, and a foreclosure judgment sets a sale 20 to 35 days out.

A person facing any of these should get the payoff, the lease or the court papers in hand before accepting an offer. A short conversation with a Florida attorney costs less than a mistake at closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Panama City house that still has storm damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Buyers who pay cash often take houses as-is, but expect the offer to reflect repair cost, and have your permit and claim records ready.

faqs.q: When is the Bay County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: Bills are due March 31 and become delinquent April 1. Paying early earns 4 percent off in November, falling one point each month through February.

faqs.q: Where do I get permit questions answered in Panama City?
faqs.a: Contact Building Services at 501 Harrison Ave. or 850-872-3025. The city's page says the owner is responsible for confirming permits.

faqs.q: Who pays doc stamps on a Panama City sale?
faqs.a: The contract decides, but the state says all parties to the document are liable. The rate printed by the statute is 70 cents per $100 of consideration.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption move with me?
faqs.a: Part of it can. Portability lets you transfer Save Our Homes savings to a new Florida homestead within three years, using Form DR-501T filed with the DR-501 by March 1.
